subject: Tiered escalation ladder & temporary on-call rollout during capacity rebalance
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@stormline.com>
Cc: support@stormline.com
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Tiered escalation ladder & temporary on-call rollout during capacity rebalance

Hi all,

Quick summary: our upcoming capacity rebalance in APAC (May 27-28 window) will reduce immediate dedicated pool capacity for several of Stormline's P1-backed endpoints. Stormline has asked for guaranteed P1/P2 response posture during the window. I want to propose a short-term operational change that preserves our P1 SLA commitments while we shift capacity. This is an exception request and requires approval from Sales and Ops.

Proposal (high level):
- Effective 2028-05-27 22:00 APAC -> 2028-05-28 06:00 APAC: enable "Tiered escalation" for Stormline routes.
  - Tier 1: On-call engineer (APAC) — 15 minute P1 response expectation.
  - Tier 2: Cross-region responder (EMEA) — 30 minute backup.
  - Tier 3: Dedicated incident lead (US) — 60 minute oversight and exec notifications.
- Temporarily increase priority paging frequency for P1 alerts on affected routes.
- Activate capacity-fallback policy to route traffic to compatible lighter-weight model variant if latency spikes > 300ms for 3 consecutive minutes.

Attachments: capacity-rebalance-runbook-v1.pdf (plan), tiered-escalation-matrix.xlsx (roles & contact ladder).

Asks:
1) Ben/Karthik/Marcus: confirm runbook & on-call roster (who will take Tier 2/3).
2) Naomi: confirm we can offer Stormline a one-time SLA memorandum for the window and any credit language.
3) Emma: confirm Stormline accepts the temporary routing fallback (light-model option) and the notification cadence.

I'll collect approvals and file a formal exception to update the customer SLA record.

Thanks,
Olga
Principal, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@stormline.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tiered escalation ladder & temporary on-call rollout during capacity rebalance

Thanks, Olga — sensible approach. A few operational notes from my side:

- Roster: I'll cover Tier 2 (EMEA) handover and can be on-call for the 22:00-02:00 APAC slice; Marcus can pick up the 02:00-06:00 shift. Karthik can be Tier 3 on standby.
- Paging: we'll move Stormline's pages to the high-frequency policy for the window and enable escalation to SMS at 2 minutes for P1s (instead of our default 5).
- Runbook tweak: suggest we add an explicit rollback trigger if the light-model fallback causes >2% accuracy regression on monitored eval prompts — that'll let Stormline opt out mid-window.

Attachment suggestion added to matrix: include phone and secondary backup for each responder.

On approvals: Naomi — can you confirm whether the onetime SLA memo needs legal sign-off or if product ops can sign?

-Ben
Senior Support Lead
From: Emma Li <emma.li@stormline.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: support@stormline.com
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 10:18:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Tiered escalation ladder & temporary on-call rollout during capacity rebalance

Hi Olga / Ben,

Thanks for the proactive plan. A couple clarifications from Stormline:
- The light-model fallback: acceptable as long as we have a clearly reported accuracy delta and can opt to pause the fallback. The rollback trigger Ben suggested sounds good.
- Paging frequency: we are comfortable with higher frequency, but please ensure we still get an in-product notification (dashboard banner) for transparency.
- SLAs & credits: we need the one-time memorandum to state whether any automatic credits would apply if our P1 response objectively misses the 15-minute window due to capacity rebalancing.

If you can send the finalized memo and runbook snippets by EOD PDT tomorrow, we'll sign and confirm.

-Emma
Director, Platform Ops
Stormline Finance
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@stormline.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tiered escalation ladder & temporary on-call rollout during capacity rebalance

Quick update — legal review not required for a one-time operational memorandum; Product Ops can sign the SLA exception if product and support agree to the rollback trigger and the listed credit language. I have drafted a short memorandum that:

- Names the exact maintenance window and fallback model variant.
- Commits to the 15/30/60 minute response posture for P1/P2 tiers for the specified window.
- States that automatic credit up to 5% of the monthly invoice is available if we fail to meet the P1 response for more than one separate incident attributable to the rebalance.

I will attach the memo + the updated escalation matrix to the Drive link and transition this to the exception workflow once you confirm the roster.

Naomi
Head of Customer Contracts
Redwood Inference
